display_heading.headline: Under Their Suits, Fantasy Is All
display_heading.deck: Three-Way Play Indicates The Japanese Are Working On Having More Fun In Bed

contact_edits.before: On the subject of good-looking shows: the Canadian Opera Company's production of Debussy's Pelleas et Melisande (director Nicholas Muni, designer Dany Lyne) ranks with the Ring and Lady Macbeth of Mtsensk among the best things to happen in the new house. A dual-levelled set, with a third layer occasionally dropped in for people to die on, conjures up both a feudal court in which the rulers prefer to keep the starving ruled down below and out of sight, and the shifts between dream and reality in a beautiful, mysterious work. Maybe the mystery turned off the first-night audience, whose response was phenomenally tepid by operatic standards. But even if diva-worship (and divoworship) is your main thing, you should be amply rewarded by Russell Braun's Pelleas, Isabel Bayrakdarian's Melisande, and above all -- certainly in acting terms -- by the great Pavlo Hunka as the jealous Golaud, working wonders with an anguished pianissimo. - Sexual Practices of the Japanese runs through May 18 at the Factory Theatre. Call 416-504-9971 for ticket information.
